- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Underestimates prices during sustained upward trends, particularly when true values rise above 65–70.
- Overestimates in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting lag or delayed reaction to news.
- When true values show strong upward momentum (e.g., >68), model tends to overshoot initially and then correct — indicating sensitivity to recent spikes.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates when prices are near historical highs, underestimates when near lows.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days — suggesting model reacts too slowly to new information.
- When true values show a sharp drop (e.g., below 60), model often fails to adjust quickly, underestimating the drop.
- Model tends to underestimate prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are trending upward — suggesting horizon bias or model decay.
